0|7ceb17e87bde79d285a8b988cfed9eaeebe60b86|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"md: Allow devices to be re-added to a read-only array.
When assembling an array incrementally we might want to make
it device available when ""enough"" devices are present
not ""all"" devices are present.
If the remaining devices appear before the array is actually used
they should be added transparently.
We do this by using the ""read-auto"" mode where the array acts like
it is read-only until a write request arrives.
Current an add-device request switches a read-auto array to active.
This means that only one device can be added after the array is first
made read-auto.  This isn't a problem for RAID5
RAID6 or RAID10.
Also we don't really want to switch the array to read-auto at all
when re-adding a device as this doesn't really imply any change.
So:
- remove the ""md_update_sb()"" call from add_new_disk().  This isn't
really needed as just adding a disk doesn't require a metadata
update.  Instead
column2: just set MD_CHANGE_DEVS.  This will effect a

column1: metadata update soon enough
column2: once the array is not read-only.

column1: - Allow the ADD_NEW_DISK ioctl to succeed without activating a
read-auto array
column2: providing the MD_DISK_SYNC flag is set.

column1: In this case
column2: the device will be rejected if it cannot be added

column1: with the correct device number
column2: or has an incorrect event count.

column1: - Teach remove_and_add_spares() to be careful about adding spares
when the array is read-only (or read-mostly) - only add devices
that are thought to be in-sync
column2: and only do it if the array is

column1: in-sync itself.
- In md_check_recovery
case
column2: rather than open coding just the 'remove' part of it.
